```{r}
#| include: false
# Shared 6-peak loader: pm (run x detector x peak archive), n_peaks, laser_of(),
# laser_levels, detector_channels. Loads ggcyto/plotly and dplyr last.
source("pages/_6peak_load.R")
# Shared Levey-Jennings helpers (add_lj_bands / lj_render): fixed robust band,
# median +/- MAD-scaled SD over the whole history, flagged points excluded.
source("pages/_lj_helpers.R")

TheDate <- format(max(pm$datetime, na.rm = TRUE), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

# Engineer visits (verticals), same source/filter as the daily-QC EVO page.
Maint <- read.csv("data/reference/AuroraMaintenance.csv", check.names = FALSE)
Maint <- Maint[Maint$instrument %in% "EVO" & !grepl("lean", Maint$reason), , drop = FALSE]
VisitTimes <- as.POSIXct(lubridate::mdy(Maint$date), tz = "UTC")

visit_layer <- function() {
  if (length(VisitTimes) == 0) return(NULL)
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(VisitTimes), colour = "steelblue",
             linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.5)
}

# One detector's LJ trend plot, shaped the way _lj_helpers.R expects:
# p$data has DateTime, a value column named exactly p$labels$title (the detector),
# and a "Flag-<detector>" logical column (flagged points are excluded from the
# band baseline and drawn as red squares).
lj_det_plot <- function(d, det, ylab) {
  d <- d[order(d$DateTime), , drop = FALSE]
  names(d)[names(d) == "value"] <- det
  names(d)[names(d) == "flag"]  <- paste0("Flag-", det)
  fl <- d[d[[paste0("Flag-", det)]] %in% TRUE, , drop = FALSE]
  ggplot(d, aes(x = DateTime, y = .data[[det]])) +
    visit_layer() +
    geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(colour = "black", size = 1.5) +
    geom_point(data = fl, colour = "red", shape = 15, size = 2.5) +
    labs(title = det, x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_bw()
}

# Per-laser named list of per-detector plots for one peak + metric.
# Flag = saturated or outside the instrument range. `resolved` (separation from the
# neighbouring peak in that detector) is deliberately NOT a flag: population labels
# come from the anchor-detector clustering, so an overlapping blank/peak in a dim
# detector is still a valid measurement of that population (~1/3 of blank points
# are "unresolved" in dim UV/V/B detectors).
build_set <- function(peak_n, metric, ylab) {
  d <- pm |>
    filter(peak == peak_n, is.finite(.data[[metric]])) |>
    transmute(detector = as.character(detector), DateTime = datetime,
              value = .data[[metric]],
              flag = !in_range | saturated)
  dets <- intersect(detector_channels, unique(d$detector))
  plots <- lapply(setNames(dets, dets), function(k)
    lj_det_plot(d[d$detector == k, c("DateTime", "value", "flag")], k, ylab))
  lapply(setNames(laser_levels, laser_levels),
         function(L) plots[laser_of(names(plots)) == L])
}

MedP6 <- build_set(n_peaks, "median", "Peak 6 median")
CvP6  <- build_set(n_peaks, "rcv",    "Peak 6 %rCV")
CvP1  <- build_set(1,       "rcv",    "Peak 1 (blank) %rCV")

# All 6 peaks' medians on one log-y plot per detector (no bands). Resolved,
# in-range peaks only; non-positive medians can't sit on a log axis.
peak_cols <- c("1" = "grey40", "2" = "#1f77b4", "3" = "#2ca02c",
               "4" = "#ff7f0e", "5" = "#9467bd", "6" = "#d62728")
all_d <- pm |>
  filter(resolved, in_range, is.finite(median), median > 0) |>
  transmute(detector = as.character(detector), DateTime = datetime,
            Median = median, Peak = factor(peak, levels = 1:n_peaks))
all_plot <- function(det) {
  d <- all_d[all_d$detector == det, , drop = FALSE]
  ggplot(d, aes(DateTime, Median, colour = Peak, group = Peak)) +
    visit_layer() +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.3) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = peak_cols, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = det, x = NULL, y = "Median (log10)") +
    theme_bw()
}
all_dets <- intersect(detector_channels, unique(all_d$detector))
MedAllPlots <- lapply(setNames(all_dets, all_dets), all_plot)
MedAll <- lapply(setNames(laser_levels, laser_levels),
                 function(L) MedAllPlots[laser_of(names(MedAllPlots)) == L])

all_render <- function(plotlist) htmltools::tagList(lapply(plotlist, ggplotly))
```

## {.sidebar}
Levey-Jennings tracking of **URCP-38-2K 6-peak Ultra Rainbow** beads on the **Cytek Aurora EVO**. Last run: **`r TheDate`** (`r n_runs` runs).

**Median column:** the **Peak 6** tabs show the median of the brightest population for each detector, one tab per laser. The **All peaks** tabs show all six population medians together (peak 1 = blank) on a log axis, with no control bands.

**rCV column:** robust %CV of **Peak 6** (brightest) and **Peak 1** (blank). The blank median sits close to zero, so its %rCV is volatile even when the absolute spread is stable. The noise-floor SD on the [main 6-peak page](AuroraEVO_6PeakUltra.qmd) is the more robust blank measure.

**Control bands:** each Peak 6 / Peak 1 plot has a centre line at the detector's robust median over the full history. Green is within ±2 SD, amber is 2–3 SD, and the red dashed lines are at ±3 SD, where SD is the MAD-scaled SD. Bands need at least 8 unflagged runs.

**Red squares** mark runs where that peak was saturated or out of range. They're plotted but left out of the band baseline. Dotted blue verticals are engineer visits.

Note: daily QC pins bead MFI by adjusting gain, so the medians are held roughly constant by design. Sustained shifts point to a QC-target or gain issue, not directly to detector health. See the [Help](help.qmd) page for more.
